title: Almost-sure L1 Gamma homogenization of stationary ergodic integral functionals with diagonal degeneracy and minimal positive and inverse moments
source_title: Stochastic homogenization of degenerate integral functionals and their Euler-Lagrange equations
author: Matthias Ruf; Thomas Ruf
difficulty_reason: The minimal moments do not provide uniform ellipticity or the higher integrability usually used to discard bad sets. The source proves weak-L1 convergence of oscillating weights and a diagonal-weight vectorial truncation, then constructs a boundary-layer blow-up lower bound compatible with those moments. Those new ingredients and the simultaneous measurable cell limit remain required after standard ergodic and selection foundations are allowed; the final Gamma-limit assembly is not admitted on its own.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Exact Theorem3.1 under Assumption1: d>=2, p>1, bounded Lipschitz D, measurable lower-semicontinuous gradient density, stationary ergodic diagonal A, integrable |A|^p and |A^{-1}|^{p/(p-1)} and Lambda. No convexity is assumed. Read complete new core14–21,23–30 and appendix measurability48–50, with exact assumptions7–10. Cell formula is simultaneous for all gradients and cubes on a common full-probability event; positivity/coercivity constants retain original moments. New vectorial truncation requires diagonal weights. The standard additive/subadditive ergodic and measurable-selection foundations remain cited. Constrained boundary/obstacle statements and Euler-Lagrange conclusions are not separately selected. All source context preserved.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: A strengthened ergodic theorem supplies weak L1 convergence of oscillating weights at the minimal moments. Weighted vector truncation and a boundary-layer blow-up construction then prove the Gamma lower bound without uniform ellipticity or convexity. These stochastic-variational constructions are above qualifying-exam analysis.
